newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares mixed in sluggish summer trade.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares mixed in sluggish summer trade.

text.p: The summer doldrums returned to the Vilnius bourse with mixed trading Wednesday as central market turnover slumped.
Brokers said bargain prices might spark some gains but that trade volume would stay listless until a new dose of liquidity found its way into the market.
Official list shares, comprising the bourse's five top blue chip stocks, advanced 4.59 points to 902.08 points.
But Group A shares slipped 5.71 points to 1871.23 points while central market turnover fell to a sluggish 319,000 litas from 618,032 litas.
"The thing that's lacking on the market is liquidity," said one broker.
Like Baltic neighbour Latvia, Lithuania's market has experienced a long, slow correction since a furious bull-run in January.
That correction has scared off many local investors and the market simply lacks enough big companies to bring in significant foreign players, analysts say.
Brokers noted that Vilniaus Bank and Hermis Bank shares, which managed to rouse the market last week, have held steady, suggesting they may have found or even surpassed their prices.
Hermis Bank was unchanged at 190.00 litas amid central market turnover of about 88,000 litas and 95,000 litas worth of block trades at the same price.
Brokers say Hermis' results and ratios suggest it is undervalued, but its price has been stifled by the overall poor performance of the bourse.
Brokers were expecting Hermis to break 200.00 litas this week but some are now saying it will have to wait for half-year results.
Vilniaus Bank traded at a steady 230.00 litas in about 20,000 litas turnover on the central market.
